function: Learns quantized phase-shift (beamfocusing) vectors of a metasurface aperture to focus power at a 3D near-field point without CSI, from measured received power (p. 3).
system: Single-RF-chain planar 3600-element programmable metasurface (100 sub-arrays of 6x6), transmissive or radiative, 2-4-bit phase shifters; single-antenna UE; 28 GHz, 4x4x3 m room (pp. 4, 10-11).
method: TD3 actor-critic deep reinforcement learning with quantizer and exact kNN action search; one agent per sub-array, trained online from a +1/-1 power-increase reward, no pretraining (pp. 8-10).
data_channel: Custom simulator, no dataset: direct plus L reflected paths, path-loss exponent 2.7, reflection coefficient 0.1, 4x4x3 m room; online learning, no 3GPP model or measurements (pp. 4, 10-11).
test_conditions: No train/test split: online training per UE position; separate runs for y = 1.4 m and 4 m, 2/3/4-bit, 36-144 sub-arrays; transfer learning is future work (pp. 11-13).
baselines: Learned: DDPG on a single sub-array (p. 11). Non-learned: none competing, only the ideal target power as reference (p. 12). Single-module versus 100 sub-arrays (p. 12).
metrics: Normalized received power density at the UE versus iterations, peak-to-ideal-target power ratio, beam focus radius (BFR), half-power beamwidth (HPBW) (pp. 11-13).
complexity: Only the proposed kNN search has an explicit order, O(kN') (p. 9); resources claimed linear in the number of elements (p. 10); no FLOPs, parameters, or runtime.
q1_support: p. 4: "We consider the multipath channel gain model between" antenna element and UE (Eq. 1), a custom direct-plus-reflections model in a 4x4x3 m room (p. 10); no standardized or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 13: "by employing various transfer learning techniques" is only future work; every configuration is trained afresh, e.g. p. 11: "the same scenario as before is repeated" for y = 4 m.
q3_support: p. 11: "TD3 outperforms DDPG in terms of both convergence speed and received power level" gives the learned baseline only; the sole non-learned reference is p. 12: "the ideal target power", an upper bound, not a competing method.
q4_support: p. 9: "the complexity of the presented knn algorithm is O(kN ′ )" gives an explicit order for the kNN step; Remark 5 (p. 10) claims linear resource scaling.
q5_support: p. 10: "default simulation parameters are listed in table I" describes a custom simulation; no code or data link appears in the 15 pages, and the only URL (ref. [51], p. 15) is a MathWorks example used for the network design.
notes: Preprint (arXiv v3) read in full, 15 pages. Area 3 because the learned agents set metasurface phase shifts, not hardware design. ris=1 is proposed because the programmable metasurface is the aperture itself (transmissive or radiative, one RF chain, p. 4), not a reflector between base station and user; reviewer to confirm. q3 is borderline: if the ideal-CSI target (p. 12) counts as a non-learned optimization baseline, q3 would be 1. q4 rests only on the O(kN') of the kNN step (p. 9).
